name: Munanna

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine who left her dull husband for a Viking pirate
drowned when a jealous new husband pushed her into a lake
returned as a crane to trouble her murderer

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Munanna is an Irish heroine in folklore. She lived with a man she found dull. She grew tired of him and looked elsewhere. She chose a Viking pirate instead. She asked the pirate to kill her husband. He agreed, and she left with him by sea. They settled in Norway. Her new husband soon feared her. He thought she might do to him what she had done before. One day they rowed out on a lake. He pushed her overboard. She drowned. Her spirit came back to trouble him. She flew about his boat in the shape of a crane. The crane is the common form of a wronged woman in Irish tale.
